PART - A 
ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT 
1. 
The following Additional Conditions of Contract shall be read in conjunction with General 
Conditions of Contract. If there are any provisions in these Additional Conditions of Contract, 
which are at variance with the provisions of General Conditions of Contract, the provisions in 
these Additional Conditions of Contract shall take precedence. 
 
2. 
INTRODUCTION: 
 
Chennai sub region office of ESIC covers the following Establishments under ARM works: - 
 
ESI Hospital at K.K Nagar, Tamil Nadu is a 1000 bedded Hospital, located in 
Chennai, Tamil Nadu having OPD/OT &24x7, Admin Block, Old Building, Staff 
Quarters and Hostels.. 
 
“Annual Repair and Maintenance of Electrical works of building including Operation of various Electro-
Mechanical, Equipment’s and plants in ESI Establishments at K.K Nagar, Chennai of Tamil Nadu Region 
for FY 2023-24”” on Percentage Rate Basis. 
 
1. ESIC Hospital & Medical College, K.K Nagar, Chennai  
2. ESIC Staff Quarters at K.K Nagar, Chennai 
 
EPI invites offer from the eligible BIDDERS on Percentage Rate Basis to execute the above 
works and detailed scope of work is mentioned in subsequent para. 
 
The Bidder shall acquaint himself by a visit to the site, with the conditions prevailing at 
site before submission of the bid. The information given here in under is for general 
guidance and shall not be contractually binding on EPI/ESIC. All relevant site data / 
information as may be necessary shall have to be obtained / collected by the Bidder. 
 
3. 
SCOPE OF WORK :  
 
The project site for the work is clear and readily available. 
 
The brief scope of work included in this tender shall include (but not limited to) “Annual Repair and 
Maintenance of Electrical works of building including Operation of various Electro-Mechanical, Equipment’s 
and plants in ESI Establishments at K.K Nagar, Chennai of Tamil Nadu Region for FY 2023-24” on Percentage 
Rate Basis. 
1. ESIC Hospital & Medical College, K.K Nagar, Chennai  
2. ESIC Staff Quarters at K.K Nagar, Chennai 
 
Works shall be carried out including all required labour, tools and tackles.

Page 4 of 28 
 
 
The scope of work is indicative but not limited to the given below." (Here in after referred to 
as “Works’). The Contractor shall execute the works as per BOQ /as per Instruction of EIC of 
EPIL/ Client Engineers on suit to site basis to meet the ESIC requirements. 
 
The contractor will be responsible for Annual Repair and Maintenance of following works in 
the ESIC Establishments / Campuses as indicated in the Bid Documents below: 
(1) Buildings Repair and Maintenance of Civil Works/Nature including materials  
(2) Building Repair and Maintenance of Electrical Works/Nature including consumables  
(3) Water Supply, Sanitary Plumbing Maintenance work  
(4) Sewage line Repair works & Sewage Disposal Work  
(5) External Service works inside campuses of ESIC Properties. 
 
a) All the essential activities required for the functional completion of each item / scope of 
work is also to be executed as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.  
b) All men, materials, machinery, tools and plants, infra-structure, resources etc., as required 
for execution of “Works” shall be provided and arranged by CONTRACTOR for their 
portion of work. The amount/rate quoted in their offer by CONTRACTOR to EPI includes 
all charges, all direct and indirect cost of works, materials, labour, tools & tackles, plant & 
equipment, all taxes, duties, levies, royalties, and labour welfare cess etc., all 
transportation charges including for cartage of issue materials, electricity and water 
charges, site offices expenses, labour camp, bank guarantee charges, insurance charges 
(up to any port of India for imported materials only), ESI/EPF/ Statutory contributions, 
preparation of all required design & detailed engineering and all required drawings etc., 
other expenses whatsoever, incurred on execution, completion and maintenance of the 
“Works” as per ‘Tender Documents’ and their own overheads and profit etc. 
CONTRACTOR shall comply with all the requirements laid down as per ‘Tender 
Documents’ as per terms, conditions, specifications, drawings, documents etc. given in 
the ‘Tender Documents’ for the completion, handing over, maintenance period etc. for the 
project. The contractor will not be allowed to take out equipment’s from the site without 
the written permission of ESIC/EPI. 
c) The contractor / vendor has to stack adequate quantity of repair & maintenance materials 
for 15 days requirement. The required stacking arrangements including Sheds, yard as 
per CPWD norms shall be made by the contractor. No extra claims in this regard shall be 
entertained. 
d) The plant & equipment once brought to site for works shall not be allowed to be removed 
without the consent of EPI. 
e) The contractor has to procure all the construction materials as per approved makes as 
mentioned in Bid Document. 
f) Water and Power for the work shall be the responsibility of the contractor. EPI shall not be 
responsible for arranging the same. 
g) The work executed by CONTRACTOR shall be subject to audit and quality control checks 
from Quality Control Division & Technical Audit of EPI, Client and chief Technical 
Examiner of Central Vigilance commission, Govt. of India. In the eventuality of any defect

Page 5 of 28 
 
/ sub-standard works as brought out in the report or noticed otherwise at any time during 
execution, maintenance period etc., the same shall be made good by the CONTRACTOR 
at no extra cost to EPI.  
h) The CONTRACTOR shall ensure compliance with all Central, State and Local laws, 
Rules, Regulations etc. as applicable or may be applicable during the course of execution, 
maintenance etc. of the works and shall indemnify EPI against any claim for damages 
whatsoever on such accounts. The CONTRACTOR shall keep EPI indemnified at all 
times against infringement of any Patent or Intellectual Property Rights. 
 
3.1. Other Conditions of Work 
 
3.1.1. The Replacement of Consumables like Bulbs, Tube-lights etc. shall be limited to areas of 
Office Buildings, Hospital Buildings, Public area of Staff Quarters only. Procurement of 
these types of consumables inside the staff quarters shall be done by the allottee 
himself. 
3.1.2. The work of essential Repair and Maintenance and operation of essential services shall 
under no circumstances be held up. 
3.1.3. For each of the properties (or a group of properties so approved by EPI/ ESIC), the 
contractor shall maintain a Complaint Book at the site and all complaints will be entered 
in the said book which shall be periodically seen by the Officers of EPI/ESIC and as soon 
as the work is completed, suitable remarks shall be given in the Register. This Register 
should also be periodically seen by the Senior Officer of EPI and signed in token of 
having seen the same. The book shall also be available for scrutiny of ESIC and / or the 
Occupier of the property and their representatives. 
3.1.4. EPI can withdraw the work from the contractor at any time after giving fifteen days’ notice 
without assigning any reason thereof. In such an event, EPI will not accept any liability 
on account of workers engaged by the contractor and on any other account. 
 
4. 
ORDER OF PRECEDENCE: 
Clause 42.1 of GCC stands amended as under: 
In case of difference, contradiction, discrepancy, dispute with regard to Conditions of 
Contract, Specifications, Drawings, Bill of Quantities and Rates quoted by the Contractor 
and other documents forming part of the contract, the following shall prevailing order of 
precedence 
4.1 
Contract Agreement which includes NIT, Special Instructions to Tenderer , 
Memorandum. 
4.2 
Letter of Intent, detailed letter of Work Order 
4.3 
Bill of Quantity/Schedule of Quantities 
4.4 
Additional Conditions of Contract (EPIL ACC) 
4.5

4.6 
CPWD Technical Specifications & DSR (Latest Edition) 
4.7

5. 
TIME SCHEDULE & PROGRESS 
 
The clause No.’ 43.0’ of General Conditions of Contract (GCC) of this Tender document 
shall be read as under: 
 
The contract period for completion of entire work under scope shall be 7.50 (Seven and 
Half) Months from the “COMMENCEMENT OF CONTRACT PERIOD” as specified. The 
contractor should complete the all works including testing of materials as per scope of BOQ 
within above specified period and as per the instructions of Engineer-in-charge. However, 
EPIL is having liberty to Pre-close or extend the completion period as per the requirement at 
any point of time during the course of the contract. 
 
6. 
COMMENCEMENT OF CONTRACT PERIOD 
 
The responsibility of the contractor shall start from the date of acceptance of LOI. The Actual 
date of start shall be considered from the date of Signing of agreement / issue of Work order.  
7. 
DEFECT LIABILITY PERIOD: 
 
Defect Liability Period as per GCC Clause No: 74.0 is stands amended as below: 
 
The Contractor shall be responsible for the rectification of defects in the works for a period  of 
06 Months (Six Months) from the date of completion of project. 
 
8. 
SECURITY DEPOSIT CUM PERFORMANCE BANK GUARANTEE Clause 9.0 of GCC is 
amended as below: 
 
8.1. In the event of award of work, contactor shall submit security deposit @ 5% (Five Percent 
only) of the contract value of the accepted tender within 21 (twenty-one) days from the 
date of issue of Letter of Intent (LOI). lf required, any extension of time beyond 21 days 
and up to 60 days may be granted by the Competent Authority. However a penal rate of 
interest @12% per annum shall be charged for the delay in submission of Security Deposit 
after 21(twenty-one) days i.e. from 22nd day to the date of submission of Security Deposit 
but within 60 days after the date of issue of PO/ LOl. Further, if 60th day happens to be 
declared holiday in the concerned office of EPl, submission of Security Deposit can be 
accepted on the next working day. The SDPG shall be submitted in the form of Bank 
Guarantee (as per format in GCC), from any Nationalized bank / Scheduled Bank / or in the 
form of Insurance Security Bonds or Account Payee Demand Draft or Fixed Deposit 
Receipt or online Payment in an acceptable form. 
 
8.2. This SDPG shall remain valid up to 90 (ninety) days after the end of defects liability period 
and shall kept valid by proper renewal till the acceptance of EPI/ESIC.

Page 7 of 28 
 
  
8.3. In case the Contractor fails to submit the Security Deposit cum Performance Guarantee of 
the requisite amount within the stipulated period or extended period, letter of intent will 
stand withdrawn and EMD of Contractor shall be forfeited. 
 
8.4. The SDPBG shall be returned to the contractor after successful completion of Defect 
Liability Period as accepted by EPIL/ESIC.  
 
9. 
RETENTION MONEY 
 
Clause no.10.0 of GCC stands amended as below. 
“The Retention Money shall be deducted from each running bill of the Contractor at 5% (five 
percent only) of the gross value of the Running Account bill. The Earnest Money Deposited 
by the tenderer in the form of Demand Draft will be treated as part of the Retention Money. 
The Retention Money shall be refunded to the Contractor upon Completion of Work or on 
payment of the amount of the final bill whichever is later. 
  
10. 
SECURED ADVANCE:(Clause no 35 of GCC): -   - NA – 
 
11. 
Mobilization Advance:(Clause no 8.0 of GCC):-   - NA- 
 
12. 
PAYMENT CONDITIONS:- 
Clause no 37.0 of GCC stands good and the following clauses are also part of that, 
12.1. Interim RA Bills in the form of monthly running bills prepared by the contractor in soft as 
well as Hard copies shall be based on the quantities executed and measured. The 
measurements accepted by the EPIL for corresponding item will be taken for payment.  
12.2. Billing - All the day to day maintenance work will be executed on the basis of the 
demand received through Complaint Form/ Call Slips and payment will be made as per 
actual execution and as per certified measurement of the executed work at site. A 
sample Complaints Form is enclosed in ANNEXURE A of Technical Specification. The 
same is to printed and kept in bulk with the concerned departments. 
12.2.1. The contractor will have to submit the bill in 02 (two) sets positively within 7th day of 
each following month with original Complaints Forms / Original call slips.  
12.2.2. Payment is to be made on submission of bill (02 sets) along with performance / 
completion certificate & necessary supporting documents after completion of work. An 
undertaking regarding compliance of all statutory liabilities i.e. minimum wages, ESI, PF 
etc. (as applicable) must have to be submitted along with bill. 
12.2.3. All the monthly operation bills of Manpower must be supported with the following 
documents- 
 Copy of work order issued by the competent authority. 
 Copy of Attendance Register / Copy of BAS Attendance signed & sealed by contractor  
 Wages slip of workers / labours signed by workers & certified by the contractor.  
 Challan of deposited amount against ESI, PF etc. against individual workers.

Page 8 of 28 
 
 GST paid challan / copy of previous month.  
 Bank statement regarding the wages paid to the workers electronically (without any type 
of cash transaction) through NEFT, RTGS or similar way. 
12.2.4. All the maintenance bills must be supported with the followings documents- 
 Work ordered issued by the competent authority. 
 Valid original work done Complaints Forms from the department concern.  
 Monthly log book record for routine checks and maintenance throughout the hospital, if 
any. 
 GST paid challan / copy of previous month.  
12.2.5. Any deduction made towards, safety, ESHS, Quality issues etc., if any, will be deducted 
from contractor on pro rata basis. 
12.2.6. Final Bill Payment shall be released upon receipt of the due deposit amount received 
from the owner / ESIC and also satisfying the submission of required documents as 
mentioned in Clause No.31 in this additional condition of contract. 
 
13. 
METHOD OF MEASUREMENT 
 
Following clauses shall be read in conjunction with Clause no 36.0 of GCC 
Mode of measurement shall be as per relevant clauses of technical specification of this 
tender. In case the same is not available the relevant IS 1200 in conjunction with IS 
3385 shall be adopted. In case the same is also not available; the standard procedure 
adopted in CPWD shall be adopted. In case the same is not available in CPWD also, 
the measurement of the work done will be based on the mutual agreement between 
EPI/ESIC and contractor. In all the above cases, the interpretation of EPI / ESIC will be 
final and binding to the contractor. 
 
Removable / dismantling and disposal of Loose concrete, if any shall be under the 
scope contractor. If contractor fails which EPI will execute the same in bidder’s risk and 
cost. 
 
14. 
Quantity, items & works as mentioned in the price bid are completely tentative in nature and 
the same have been derived on the basis of last few years demand of the hospital & 
execution at site which may increase/ decrease or deviate from the given Quantity, items & 
works. However, prior approval should be taken from EPI/ESIC for any abnormal variation in 
quantities even if the situation warrants.  
 
 
15. 
TAXES AND DUTIES: 
 
The following shall be also read in conjunction with clause no 13 of GCC: 
15.1.1. 
The bidder/Contractor must be registered with GST and should have valid GSTIN 
number of the respective state of the project.

Page 9 of 28 
 
15.1.2. 
The bidder/contractor must submit as a compliance of GST Act, the invoices in 
GST compliant format. 
 
15.1.3. 
Contractor’s price/rates shall be inclusive of all taxes and including GST 
@18%. Contractor shall submit to EPI the GST compliant tax invoice/debit 
note/revised tax invoice on the basis of which EPI will claim the input tax credit in its 
return. Since this is a works contract, the GST rate shall be as applicable presently. 
 
15.1.4. 
GST charged in the tax invoice/debit note/revised tax invoice by the contractor 
shall be released separately to the contractor only after contractor files the outward 
supply details in GSTR-1 on GSTN portal and input tax credit of such invoice is 
matched with time of filing the monthly return. TDS under GST shall be deducted at 
prevailing rates on gross invoice value from the running bills). 
 
15.1.5. 
Labourcess / LWF- Labour welfare fund shall be deposited by EPI @ 1% of value 
of work done or as applicable from to time as per the directions of Government of 
Tamil Nadu by EPI. However, all the documentations and Labour records shall be 
maintained properly by the contractor. It shall be produced to EPI / MSME / Govt 
Authorities as and when is required. 
 
15.1.6. 
Seigniorage / Royalty Charges: The rate quoted by bidder shall be inclusive of 
all royalty / seigniorages. If any royalty/ fee is payable to local authority, such royalty/ 
fee shall also be borne by the Contractor. Disposal shall be carried out strictly as per 
the regulations of local authority. However, the above materials shall not be removed 
out of Site premises without prior written authorization of the Project Manager. 
 
15.1.7. 
The contractor shall keep necessary books of accounts and other documents for 
the purpose of this condition as may be necessary and shall allow inspection of the 
same by a duly authorized representative of EPI and shall also furnish such other 
information/document as EPI may require from time to time 
 
15.1.8. 
The contractor shall keep necessary books of accounts and other documents for 
the purpose of this condition as may be necessary and shall allow inspection of the 
same by a duly authorized representative of EPI and shall also furnish such other 
information/document as EPI may require from time to time. 
 
15.1.9. 
In case of any reduction in rate of taxes in future or the project getting exemption 
status prior to the last date of Bid submission or afterwards, the contractor shall pass 
on the benefit to EPIL immediately, failing which EPIL shall have the right to recover

Page 10 of 28 
 
the differential amount from the amounts due to the contractor. Further in case of any 
increase in rate of taxes in future or the project losing exemption status prior to last 
date of bid submission or afterwards, the said increase of taxes shall be paid / 
reimbursed to the contractor, subject to the conditions that the client reimburses the 
said increased taxes to EPIL. 
 
15.1.10. The rates quoted by the contractor shall be inclusive of all taxes and duties. 
However such duties, taxes, levies, etc. which shall be notified after the last date of 
submission of bid and/or any increase/decrease over the rate existing on the last date 
of submission of Bid shall be reimbursed/recovered by the company on production of 
documentary evidence in support of payment actually made to the concerned 
authorities subject to reimbursed the same by client. 
 
15.1.11.  
16. 
INSURANCE 
The following shall be also read in conjunction with GCC clause no.17 
 CAR Policy & ER Policy   –NA-. 
 However the bidder should submit the WC policy as per standard   
 
16.1. THIRD PARTY INSURANCE 
Contractor is required to take third party insurance cover for an amount of 5%(five percent) 
of Contract Value from an Approved Insurance Company for insurance against any 
damage, injury or loss which may occur to any person or property including that of EPI, 
arising out of the execution of the works or temporary works. Wherever required by EPI the 
Contractor shall produce the policy or the policies of Insurance and the receipt of payment 
of the current premiums. 
 
17. 
PRICE VARIATION: 
Clause 16.0 of GCC of EPI stands good. 
 
17.1. No escalation / price variation clause shall be applicable on this contract. All rates as per 
Bill of Quantities (BOQ)/Price-Bid quoted by Contractor shall be firm and fixed for entire 
contract period as well as extended period for completion of the works. No claim on account 
of any Price Variation / Escalation on whatsoever ground shall be entertained at any stage 
of works. 
 
18. 
QUANTITY VARIATION: 
 
Following clauses shall be read in conjunction with Clause no 69.1 of GCC 
 
18.1. Quantity, items & works as mentioned in the price bid are completely tentative in nature

Page 11 of 28 
 
and the same have been derived on the basis of last few years demand of the hospital & 
execution at site which may increase/ decrease or deviate from the given Quantity, items & 
works. The quantities given in the contract may change to any extent (both in plus 
side and minus side). The quoted rates for individual items shall remain firm irrespective of 
any variations in the individual quantities.  
 
18.2. No compensation becomes payable in case the variation of the final executed contract 
value is within the limit of plus/Minus (+/-) 20% Twenty Percentage)of awarded contract 
value. 
 
 
19. 
PAYMENT AGAINST EXTRA / SUPPLEMENTARY ITEMS: 
Following clauses shall be read in conjunction with Clause no 69.0 of GCC 
 
19.1. No extra items shall be executed unless and until written instructions are issued by the 
EPIL. Any extra item (including variation in specifications of listed item) executed by the 
contractor without the permission in writing shall not be payable. In case of extra items, 
contractor shall furnish detailed breakup of the rate of extra item with supporting documents 
with detailed cost break up duly signed by Engineer-in-Charge of EPIL, which shall be got 
approved from the Competent Authority 
 
19.2. In case of any emergency works arise / situation warrants at any establishment against 
complaints / end users/ ESIC/EPIL, which are not in original agreement /BOQ , which shall 
be  carried out (if needed) as DSR/SSR/MR analysis with the consent of Engineer –in- 
charge of EPIL. 
 
19.3. Latest CPWD Schedule Rate (1st preference)/ latest PWD Schedule Rate, TWAD Board 
Rate, TN (2nd preference)/ Market Rate [for the item which are not available at CPWD/ 
PWD Schedule] (3rd preference) will be considered for finalizing item rate not in the BOQ.  
 
19.4. Once EPI receives the approval and corresponding payment from ESIC, the same shall 
be passed on to contractor as per above clause. 
 
20. 
Land for material yard shall be provided within the site premises after approval of Client. In 
case, due to any reason land could not available for the same purpose. In such case, 
contractor should arrange himself for the same purpose no claims shall be entertained in this 
regard. 
 
21. 
Furnished Office Accommodation & Mobility and Communication to be provide by Contractor 
to EPI – the GCC Clause No. 28.3 stands deleted.  
 
22. 
PROTECTION OF TREES – GCC Clause No. 28.50 stands good. 
 
23. 
FREE ISSUE OF MATERIAL-               NA

Page 12 of 28 
 
 
24. 
WATER &ELECTRICITY –Clause no 44.0 of GCC stands good. 
 
25. 
COMPENSATION FOR DELAY:  
Clause no.72.1of GCC for compensation for delay (Liquidity Damages) stands good. 
If the Contractor fails to maintain the required progress in terms of clause 72.4 or relevant 
clause of Additional Conditions of Contract, to complete the work and clear the Site on or before 
the completion date or extended date of completion, he shall, without prejudice to any other right 
or remedy available under the law to EPI on account of such breach, pay as agreed 
compensation the amount calculated at the rates stipulated below or such smaller amount as 
the Engineer in charge (whose decision in writing shall be final and binding) may decide on the 
amount of tendered value of the work for every completed day / week (as applicable) that the 
progress remains below that specified in Clause 72.4.1 or the relevant clause in Additional 
Conditions of Contract or that the work remains incomplete. This will also apply to items or 
group of items for which a separate period of completion has been specified. 
i) For works with completion period not exceeding 3 month (as originally stipulated) @ 1% per 
day 
ii) For works with completion period exceeding 3 months (as originally stipulated) @ 1% per 
week or part thereof  
Provided always that the total amount of compensation for delay to be paid under this Condition 
shall not exceed 10% of the Tendered Value of work or of the Tendered Value of the item or 
group of items of work for which a separate period of completion is originally given. 
The amount of compensation may be adjusted or set-off against any sum payable to the 
Contractor under this or any other contract with EPI even after completion of the work. 
 
26. 
CANCELLATION/DETERMINATION OF CONTRACT IN FULL OR PART 
Clause no 72.2 of GCC stands good 
 
27. 
CONTRACTOR LIABLE TO PAY COMPENSATION EVEN IF ACTION NOT TAKEN 
Clause no 72.3 of GCC stands good 
 
28. 
TIME ESSENCE OF CONTRACT & EXTENSION FOR DELAY 
Clause no 72.4 of GCC stands good  
 
Extension of time for completion 
The contract period may be extended / pre-closed as per the requirement of EPI/ESIC. The 
Repair and Maintenance contract may be extended on the written mutual consent of both EPIL 
and Contractor for a further reasonable period.  However, employer reserves to right to 
terminate the Repair and Maintenance contract by giving 15 days notice at any time during the 
currency of the contract if the services of the agency are not satisfactory as per the opinion of 
employer or its representative.

Page 13 of 28 
 
 
 
29. 
COMPLETION AND TAKING OVER 
 
As soon as the project is completed including extended period if any, EPI/ESIC shall 
nominate their Officers for checking /Verification of completed work as per the scope of 
work and terms and conditions and compliance of statutory compliances etc., for 
financial closure. 
 
A final certificate of rectification of all defects pointed out by the handing over taking 
overboard shall be obtained by the contractor.  
 
30. 
FINAL BILL: The final bill will be submitted by the contractor within 90 days from the date of 
acceptance of completion of work accompanied by the following documents: 
30.1. Completion certificate (or) Final Acceptance Certificate issued by the EPI/ESIC 
specifying the handing over of the work including list of inventories (fittings & fixtures). 
30.2. No claim certificate by the Contactor. 
30.3. Duly approved by the EPI/ESIC ‘As built’ drawings in required sets if any & if applicable. 
30.4. Certified Measurements for the work executed. 
30.5. All statutory approvals from various state/central govt. local bodies, if required for 
completion & handing over of the work as included in scope of Contractor. 
30.6. Manufacture’s guarantee of various machines / equipment’s installed as part of works if 
any. 
 
31. 
DRAWINGS: 
 
The detailed drawings, specifications if any available with EPI, the same will be made 
available to the contract or during execution of work at site. 
 
32. 
TECHNICAL STAFF FOR WORK: 
 
Clause 27.0 of GCC stands modified as under. 
 
The Contractor shall employ at his cost the adequate number of technical staff (apart from 
the number of staff /operators mentioned in BOQ) during the execution of this work 
depending upon the requirement of work. For this purpose the numbers to be deployed, their 
qualification, experience as decided by EPI shall be final and binding on Contractor. The 
Contractor shall not be entitled for any extra payment in this regard. The technical staff 
should be available at Site, whenever required by EPI to take instructions.

33. 
LABOUR CAMP: 
 
The Contractor shall be responsible for accommodation, feeding and sanitary necessities, 
for their employed persons. The Contractor shall make his own arrangement for labour 
camp for his labour. No labour camp shall be allowed inside the project site. EPIL shall not 
provide land for labour camp. 
 
34. 
TESTS AND INSPECTION: 
 
34.1. Clause no 53.1 of GCC stands good and in addition to that the following shall be 
applicable. Lab/testing equipment if any have to be procured and installed by contractor, if 
required. Later on expenditure can be shared after other contractor deployed. 
34.2. All works executed or under the course of execution in pursuance of this contract shall at 
all times be open to inspection and supervision of EPI. The work during its progress or after 
its completion may also be inspected, by Chief Technical Examiner of Government of India 
(CTE) and/ or an inspecting authority of State Government of State in which work is 
executed and/or by third party checks by Owner/ Clients. The compliance of observations/ 
improvements as suggested by the inspecting officers of EPI/CTE/ State authorities/ 
Owners shall be obligatory on the part of the Contractor at the cost of Contractor. Any 
recovery, penalty imposed by CTE due to non-performance, noncompliance of agreed 
condition or otherwise whatsoever the same shall be recovered from RA Bill of contractor. 
 
35. 
BLASTING:   NA 
 
 
 
36. 
PRIORITY OF WORK:  
The contractor has to deploy resources and plan the work accordingly and nothing extra 
shall be payable to the contractor on this account. The contractor has to ensure safety of the 
occupants as to avoid any hazard to occupants. 
 
37. 
GATEPASS AND PERMITS:  
The contractor shall make own arrangements for obtaining the necessary gate pass / entry 
and exit permits for men, material, labours and construction machinery etc as applicable/ 
required to complete the work without any extra cost to EPI..     
 
38. 
TOOLS AND PLANTS/ MONITORING AND MEASURING EQUIPMENT(MMEs) 
 
Bidder/ Contractor should have their own minimum Tools and Plants for their Day to Day

plant and machineries required to complete the work without any extra cost to EPI. 
 
Bidder/ Contractor shall have their own Mobile scaffolding /staging system as part of their 
tools and plants for to carry out their day to day, periodical maintenance works.
